# pg-sse-client

> JavaScript/TypeScript client for pg-sse streams (the Python library that sends server-sent events from Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY). `EventSource` on top of `fetch`: it can send headers, and it keeps what pg-sse's contract needs from `EventSource` (resume from the last id, the server's reconnect delay, the goodbye frame). Browser and Node 20+, ESM only, no dependencies.

Install: `npm install pg-sse-client`. Not the unrelated `pg-sse` package on npm.

Rules when generating code with pg-sse-client:

- Use plain `new EventSource(url)` when the stream authenticates with a same-origin cookie or `withCredentials`: it reconnects and sends `Last-Event-ID` by itself. Use this package to send a header (`Authorization`), to read a token that changes between attempts, to see why a stream ended or was refused, or to decide what to do after repeated failures.
- `const stream = connect(url, { onEvent, ...options })` starts at once, like `new EventSource`. `stream.close()` ends it for good and is the cleanup (return `() => stream.close()` from a React effect). `stream.retryNow()` cuts a wait short. `stream.lastEventId` is the cursor.
- `url` is a string, a `URL`, or a function `(lastEventId) => string | URL` called before every attempt. A string or `URL` that cannot be fetched, `headers` given as a value that cannot be sent, and any `cursorIn` but `'header'` or `'url'` throw `TypeError` from `connect`.
- Auth: `headers: async () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${await getToken()}` })`, called before every attempt. `Accept` and `Last-Event-ID` are the client's; put no `Last-Event-ID` in `headers`.
- Cross-origin: `Last-Event-ID` needs `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Last-Event-ID` on the server (and `Authorization` if sent), or the first reconnect fails. Without that, `cursorIn: 'url'` with a URL function carries the cursor in the query and sends no header: `connect((id) => `${base}?cursor=${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, { cursorIn: 'url', onEvent })`. `cursorIn: 'url'` needs a URL function. The function gets the cursor (`''` at first) whatever `cursorIn` is.
- `onEvent(event)` gets `{ event, data, id }` for every event but the goodbye; `data` is a string, so `JSON.parse(event.data)`. A callback that throws or rejects does not stop the stream: the error goes to `onCallbackError(error)`, else a page or worker rethrows it to `window.onerror` and anything else logs it with `console.error`.
- The goodbye is the event named `endEvent` (default `end`, the hub's `end_event`): `onEnd(reason)` (`max_age`, `shutdown`, `behind`, `revoked`, `recheck`, or any other string; `unknown` when it has no reason), then it reconnects. It is not passed to `onEvent`; an app event of your own named `end` would be taken for it, so name yours otherwise or set `endEvent`.
- Callbacks: `onOpen()`, `onDisconnect()` (a stream that had opened has ended, before `onError`; not called by `close()`), `onEnd(reason)`, `onError(error, { failures })`, `onClose(error?)` (over for good: no argument after `close()`, the error otherwise; once).
- `onError` hears every failed attempt and returns `'retry'`, `'stop'`, `{ retryAfterMs, wakeOnResume? }` or nothing (the default), and may be `async`. Default: stop on a 4xx other than 408 and 429 (a 401 too: return `'retry'` for it when `headers` can get a fresh token), on a 3xx that was not followed, on a 2xx that is not `text/event-stream`, and on `SseEventTooLarge`; retry everything else. `{ retryAfterMs }` waits that long, never less than the server's `Retry-After` or last `retry:`, and resets `failures`; `wakeOnResume: true` also ends the rest when the browser comes back `online` or the tab becomes visible, after the first second and that floor.
- Polling fallback: `onError: (error, { failures }) => { if (failures >= 3) { startPolling(); return { retryAfterMs: 180_000, wakeOnResume: true }; } }` and `onOpen: stopPolling`.
- Errors are classes: `StreamRefused` (`status`, `retryAfterMs`), `StreamTimeout` (`phase`: `'connect'` or `'idle'`), `StreamEndedEarly` (`lastedMs`, `reason`: a stream closed within `backoff.shortMs`, 5 s, counts as a failure), `SseEventTooLarge` (`limit`, `events`). Anything else is what `fetch` threw.
- Reconnecting: after a stream open 5 s or more the wait is the stream's `retry:`, else 0.5 to 2 s at random. After a failure it doubles from 1 s to 30 s with jitter, never under the last `retry:` or a `Retry-After` (both capped at `backoff.serverMaxMs`, 1 hour). `backoff` takes `baseMs`, `maxMs`, `shortMs`, `reconnectFloorMs`, `reconnectSpreadMs`, `serverMaxMs`; an entry that is not a finite number of at least 0 keeps its default.
- Timeouts: `connectTimeoutMs` (15000, the `headers` function included) and `idleTimeoutMs` (45000, pings count); 0 or a value too long for a timer turns one off.
- `lastEventId` resumes from there on the first attempt. `init` is more `fetch` options (`credentials`, `mode`); `method`, `headers`, `body` and `signal` are the client's. `fetch` replaces the global one and is called with no receiver. `maxEventChars` (no limit by default, or when 0) caps how much of one event is held.
- Only the parser, for a stream you open yourself (a `POST` that answers with events): `import { createSseParser, readSse } from 'pg-sse-client/parser'`; `for await (const event of readSse(response.body, onActivity))`. To resume use the `id` of the last event you handled, not `parser.lastEventId`.
- Not here: the meaning of your events (that is your server's protocol), a message queue (the server re-reads from the cursor it was sent), and any framework binding.

Full reference: https://github.com/sansanth/pg-sse-client#readme
